finding.claim: When a caller passes subject= to decode(), _validate_sub silently accepts issuer-signed tokens that have no sub claim, unlike aud and iss which raise MissingRequiredClaimError when the claim is absent.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token validly signed by the same key/issuer but lacking a sub claim (e.g. a service or other token class sharing the key).
finding.sink: Subject-bound authorization check performed by the caller via decode(..., subject=...) (api_jwt.py:421 -> 452-454).

trace.note: Returns early when 'sub' not in payload, before the subject comparison

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification runs first (api_jws.py:277-285) so the token is issuer-signed. verify_sub default True. Sibling validators fail closed: _validate_aud raises MissingRequiredClaimError when aud absent (api_jwt.py:529-532); _validate_iss raises when iss absent (api_jwt.py:571-572). jwt/types.py:51 documents sub check as applying 'if present in payload', so behaviour is documented, making this a footgun rather than a silent bug. Mitigation: require=['sub'] or an application-side payload.get('sub') check.
